craft_notes: Sthāyin: rati sharpened by viyoga — verse color is violence inside tenderness (bank rasa for this verse: śṛṅgāra turning to vīra). Sanskrit first: manmathe ca hṛdi hantum udyate / proṣitapramadayedam udyate — yamaka pair udyate×udyate closing both halves; two arisings, one event (argmap INF). Firing rows: row 9 (yamaka → anaphora rises…rises, inherited from frozen L3, kept whole — the pair IS the verse); row 8 (vowel music: with→beside at the close-swell — long vowel lets the line breathe where with-him dies short; bright kill against soft beside-him enacts rati softening vīra at the close); close-shape arrested not settled (the wound opens here; the song settles only at v9's question). ONE-WORD edit from L3, same ids, same doctrine (one-event): beside holds nearness (rati) where him merely points. Read aloud: two balanced breaths, dash caesuras, the second line landing longer and softer — the killer sung tender. REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) L3 verbatim 'rises with him' → killed: dull short-vowel close; music asks the lift, doctrine unchanged so the edit is free. (b) bank's 'wakes to kill' → killed: L3 froze the rises/rises yamaka-pair; breaking one end breaks both. (c) quatrain split (one arising per couplet) → killed by argmap one-event: splitting unmakes the oneness. (d) exclamatory 'to kill!' → killed: cold statement is crueler; heat would be imported vighna. (e) 'parted'→'separated' (L2/bank word) → killed: L3 frozen, both trace identically.

lines: In the heart, Kāma rises to kill —
and the parted beloved rises beside him.
